kb.title: How to import a STM32CubeMX2 CMake project into STM32CubeIDE
kb.content_text:
## Summary

This guide explains how to take an existing **STM32CubeMX2** project, generate a **CMake** project from it, and then import it into **STM32CubeIDE**.

## **Prerequisites**

* [STM32CubeIDE version 2.1.1](https://www.st.com/en/development-tools/stm32cubeide.html)

* [STM32CubeMX2 version 1.0.0](https://www.st.com/en/development-tools/stm32cubemx.html)

## 1. Generate a CMake project from STM32CubeMX2

1. Create an **STM32CubeMX2** .ioc project.

2. In **Project Manager → IDE Project** (IDE Project Generation area), set:

* **Format:** CMake

* **CMake toolchain:** GCC

* **Destination:** a folder where the CMake project should generate.

3. Click **Generate IDE project**.

When generation completes, verify that the destination folder contains:

* CMakeLists.txt

* Core/, Drivers/, and other generated folders.

* The .ioc file.

![Figure 1. IDE project generation](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/7d750259-6e94-01b6-7ee1-2f3b6426fd9e.png "Mohamed_BACHOUCH_5-1774454987450.png")Figure 1. IDE project generation

## 2. Open the STM32CubeMX2 CMake project in STM32CubeIDE

1. Launch **STM32CubeIDE V2.1.1** and select your workspace.

2. From the main menu, choose:

**[File] → [New] → [STM32 Project] → [STM32 Project Create/Import]**.

Select **[****STM32CubeMX2 project]**under **[****Create New STM32 Project]**.

![Figure 2. Import STM32 project](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/6ee2f5d3-a7b9-1229-8ba0-eba2fb5e2019.png "1.png")Figure 2. Import STM32 project

![Figure 3. Import STM32CubeMX2 project](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/fe80a3f3-a421-71e9-f6db-06fd4411438c.png "2.png")Figure 3. Import STM32CubeMX2 project

## 3. Point the project to the existing CMake sources

You are now on the **Project with existing CMake sources** page. Fill in the fields as follows:

* **Project name**

Enter a name for your STM32CubeIDE project.

* **Source directory**

Click **[****Browse...]**, and select the folder generated in section 1.

![Figure 4. Point the project to the existing CMake sources](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/057fc3ff-0e02-fe29-5be4-fcd85c111b2c.png "3.png")Figure 4. Point the project to the existing CMake sources

## 4. Configure the toolchain and MCU

The wizard opens the "**Configure default tool‑chain settings for the project"**page.

1. Configure:

* **Toolchain:** MCU ARM GCC (or matching your setup).

* **MCU:** Select the same device as in the STM32CubeMX2 project.

* **Example used**: STM32C562VETx.

2. Click **Finish**.

![Figure 5. Configure the toolchain and MCU](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/730ca86e-0362-d4db-dc42-b21917e4d4f4.png "4.png")Figure 5. Configure the toolchain and MCU

## 5. Build and use the imported project

In "**Project Explorer"**, the new STM32 CMake project should be visible:

* CMakeLists.txt at the root.

* Core/, Drivers/, and other generated folders.

**[Right‑click]** the project → **[****Build Project]**.

STM32CubeIDE runs CMake, configures the build system, and compiles the code.

## Related links

* [STM32CubeIDE](https://www.st.com/en/development-tools/stm32cubeide.html)

* [STM32CubeMX2](https://www.st.com/en/development-tools/stm32cubemx.html)
